doctrine: Canonical current-loss accounting covers standing material loss/damage as of the analytical cutoff. Eight material-loss categories use bounded procurement, capability-analogue, composition, or severity models. MUNITIONS_EXPENDITURE is a separate accounting product for weapons intentionally expended on launch. Hypothetical future repair/reconstitution spending is excluded from canonical current-loss accounting.
double_counting_rule: Material-loss aggregate sums only the eight categories explicitly marked ADDITIVE_TO_MATERIAL_LOSS_TOTAL and constructed to exclude cross-category components. MUNITIONS_EXPENDITURE remains separate. Destroyed inventory before use and intentionally expended weapons are not merged without item-level deconfliction.

envelopes.label: CONSERVATIVE EVIDENCE-SUPPORTED FLOOR
envelopes.quantity_basis: CSIS observed-loss floor extended to 2 power-projection/AFSB hulls and 30 mine-laying small craft.
envelopes.methodology: Component build-up. Existing frigate/corvette/FAC/submarine analogues are retained. AFSB hulls are anchored to a $56M-$58M 2010 Aframax market value and apply explicit conversion/mission-system premiums. ONI shows Ashoora mine-layers are standard small boats with mine rails, so they are modeled as small-craft rather than full-size minelayers.
exclusions: Support ships not itemized by class
onboard weapons already embedded in full-program combatant analogues where applicable

envelopes.methodology: Component build-up. Existing frigate/corvette/FAC/submarine analogues are retained. AFSB hulls are anchored to a $56M-$58M 2010 Aframax market value and apply explicit conversion/mission-system premiums. ONI shows Ashoora mine-layers are standard small boats with mine rails, so they are modeled as small-craft rather than full-size minelayers.

overlap_notes: Port/shipyard civil damage is in FIXED_INFRASTRUCTURE, not here.
Salvage/clearance is excluded from hull replacement; future restoration spending is outside canonical current-loss accounting.

envelopes.label: CONSERVATIVE EVIDENCE-SUPPORTED FLOOR
envelopes.quantity_basis: Observed/independently reported aircraft set using 2 F-14 floor plus fixed losses documented in imagery/reporting.
envelopes.methodology: Historical acquisition/CPI proxies retained for F-14/F-4/F-5. TWZ/Vantor provides the 10 F-7, Il-76, two C-130, two Su-22, two Su-24 and Yak-130 loss set. exclusions: Unknown additional F-5/F-27 parked-aircraft losses at Ahvaz beyond the two Tabriz F-5s

envelopes.label: CONSERVATIVE EVIDENCE-SUPPORTED FLOOR
envelopes.quantity_basis: Known prewar system mix multiplied by an 80% destruction-equivalent campaign floor; indigenous unknown-count families excluded.
envelopes.methodology: Iran-specific procurement anchors are used where public (five S-300 battalions >$800M; 29 Tor-M1 for $700M). CSIS supplies prewar system counts. Legacy/indigenous systems lacking contracts use explicit capability bands below/around modern imported systems. The 80% campaign destruction assessment is applied as a terminal-equivalent fraction, not as proof that 80% of every named family was destroyed.

envelopes.label: CENTRAL MODELED ESTIMATE
envelopes.quantity_basis: Known systems plus 30 indigenous mid-range system equivalents; 80% destruction-equivalent.
envelopes.methodology: Iran-specific procurement anchors are used where public (five S-300 battalions >$800M; 29 Tor-M1 for $700M). CSIS supplies prewar system counts. Legacy/indigenous systems lacking contracts use explicit capability bands below/around modern imported systems. The 80% campaign destruction assessment is applied as a terminal-equivalent fraction, not as proof that 80% of every named family was destroyed.

envelopes.label: ASSESSED UPPER ENVELOPE
envelopes.quantity_basis: Known systems plus 60 indigenous mid-range and 20 fixed radar equivalents; 90% severity to bound campaign-level claims.
envelopes.methodology: Iran-specific procurement anchors are used where public (five S-300 battalions >$800M; 29 Tor-M1 for $700M). CSIS supplies prewar system counts. Legacy/indigenous systems lacking contracts use explicit capability bands below/around modern imported systems. The 80% campaign destruction assessment is applied as a terminal-equivalent fraction, not as proof that 80% of every named family was destroyed.

overlap_notes: Air-defense launchers/radars are included here. LAUNCHERS below is ballistic-missile TELs only.
Fixed building shells are not included.

envelopes.label: CONSERVATIVE EVIDENCE-SUPPORTED FLOOR
envelopes.quantity_basis: >335 launchers neutralized; conservative 60% terminal-equivalent share.
envelopes.methodology: Reuters reports Israeli officials said >335 missile launchers were neutralized. Exact Iranian TEL families and recoverability are unknown, so the model uses $2M/$4M/$6M per TEL-equivalent. The $6M upper is anchored to the U.S. Army FY2023 HIMARS launcher recurring cost (~$5.625M) as a modern mobile-launcher capability analogue; low/central explicitly discount for simpler Iranian platforms.

envelopes.label: CENTRAL MODELED ESTIMATE
envelopes.quantity_basis: >335 launchers neutralized; 80% terminal-equivalent central share.
envelopes.methodology: Reuters reports Israeli officials said >335 missile launchers were neutralized. Exact Iranian TEL families and recoverability are unknown, so the model uses $2M/$4M/$6M per TEL-equivalent. The $6M upper is anchored to the U.S. Army FY2023 HIMARS launcher recurring cost (~$5.625M) as a modern mobile-launcher capability analogue; low/central explicitly discount for simpler Iranian platforms.

envelopes.label: ASSESSED UPPER ENVELOPE
envelopes.quantity_basis: Treats 335 as fully replacement-equivalent at a unit band slightly above the FY2023 HIMARS recurring launcher cost.
envelopes.methodology: Reuters reports Israeli officials said >335 missile launchers were neutralized. overlap_notes: This category is ballistic-missile TELs only; SAM launchers remain inside AIR_DEFENSE_RADAR.

envelopes.label: CONSERVATIVE EVIDENCE-SUPPORTED FLOOR
envelopes.quantity_basis: Lowest prewar missile-stock estimate (2,500) × one-third certainly destroyed ≈ 833 missiles. No additive destroyed-UAS airframe quantity is modeled because Reuters describes roughly one-third of drone capability destroyed, not an itemized physical airframe inventory.
envelopes.methodology: Reuters reports U.S. intelligence certainty that about one-third of Iran's missile arsenal was destroyed. Reuters separately describes another third as mixed status—damaged, destroyed, or buried/inaccessible—and says some buried or damaged missiles may be recoverable. Low and central therefore count only the certainly-destroyed one-third. The upper envelope counts the certainly-destroyed one-third plus a 50% replacement-equivalent severity factor on the ambiguous second third; this 50% is an explicit analyst midpoint for a mixed physical-damage/inaccessibility tranche and is not a claim that half the missiles are known destroyed. Temporary inaccessibility is never valued at 100% replacement loss. Reuters' separate 'one-third of drone capability destroyed' assessment is not converted into an airframe quantity; destroyed UAS inventory receives no separate additive dollar line absent a defensible physical count.
exclusions: UAS physical-airframe inventory quantity not separately priced because the available assessment is capability-based rather than an itemized prewar airframe inventory.
Temporary missile inaccessibility/burial without demonstrated physical damage.
Expended missiles/UAS counted separately in MUNITIONS_EXPENDITURE.
Production machinery and facility damage counted separately in INDUSTRIAL_PRODUCTION/FIXED_INFRASTRUCTURE.

envelopes.label: ASSESSED UPPER ENVELOPE
envelopes.quantity_basis: Upper prewar stock (6,000). One-third (2,000) is treated as certainly destroyed. A second one-third is Reuters' mixed-status tranche (damaged, destroyed, or buried/inaccessible); only 50% of that tranche is counted as replacement-equivalent physical loss/damage (1,000 missile-equivalents). The remaining ambiguous/inaccessible half is tracked as degraded/inaccessible capability and excluded from material-loss dollars.

overlap_notes: Destroyed missile inventory only is additive here; intentionally expended missiles/UAS remain in MUNITIONS_EXPENDITURE.
UAS capability degradation is retained analytically but no physical airframe quantity is monetized absent a defensible inventory derivation.
Industrial-production/facility losses are separate and must not be used as a proxy count for destroyed UAS airframes.

missile_physical_loss_scope.upper_case_reason: Reuters says the second third mixes physical damage/destruction with burial/inaccessibility and that some buried/damaged missiles may be recoverable. A 50% replacement-equivalent severity factor prevents automatic 100% loss treatment while preserving a bounded physical-damage allowance.
missile_physical_loss_scope.non_additive_degraded_or_inaccessible_sh: Any ambiguous share not represented by the 50% damage-equivalent factor remains capability degradation/inaccessibility, not standing material loss.

uas_physical_inventory_treatment.assessment: Reuters reports some degree of intelligence certainty that roughly one-third of Iranian drone capability had been destroyed.
uas_physical_inventory_treatment.reason: The source is capability-based, not an itemized prewar physical-airframe inventory. Converting it to 1,500/3,000/4,500 destroyed airframes would manufacture quantity precision and risks overlap with INDUSTRIAL_PRODUCTION damage.
uas_physical_inventory_treatment.overlap_control: Do not monetize a destroyed-UAS airframe inventory unless a separately sourced physical prewar inventory and destroyed-airframe derivation are added and deconflicted from industrial-production/facility losses.

envelopes.label: CONSERVATIVE EVIDENCE-SUPPORTED FLOOR
envelopes.quantity_basis: Prices mission-system/secure-fitout equivalents for a conservative subset of verified command/HQ incidents.
envelopes.methodology: Bellingcat verified 29 command-center/HQ incidents in the police/security infrastructure set; CSIS separately documents military/naval C2 damage. Patton Hall ($100M complete C2 HQ) is used as a high-end facility analogue. To avoid overlap with FIXED_INFRASTRUCTURE, this category prices only secure communications, operations-room, mission-system and specialized fitout equivalents, not building shells.

envelopes.label: CENTRAL MODELED ESTIMATE
envelopes.quantity_basis: Prices mission-system/secure-fitout equivalents for 18 ordinary and 3 high-level/hardened nodes.

envelopes.label: CONSERVATIVE EVIDENCE-SUPPORTED FLOOR
envelopes.quantity_basis: Civil/structural floor across documented naval-port, airbase/security, industrial-shell and hardened-site damage.
envelopes.methodology: Class-based civil/reconstruction build-up. World Bank Karachi project provides a 922m quay-wall reconstruction analogue ($112.6M in 2010 project terms). Iran-local public construction rates in iran-war-cost-estimate.json constrain ordinary shell costs. CSIS documents major damage at Bandar Abbas, Bushehr, Anzali, Chabahar/Konarak and weapons-production sites. Values are scenario classes because exact damage polygons are incomplete.
exclusions: dredging beyond explicitly bounded port-work scenarios

envelopes.label: CONSERVATIVE EVIDENCE-SUPPORTED FLOOR
envelopes.quantity_basis: 12 terminal-equivalent specialized production lines plus limited shipyard specialty-equipment burden.
envelopes.methodology: CENTCOM/Reuters and AP report broad attacks on missile, drone, naval production and shipyards; CSIS imagery confirms damage to aboveground weapon-production sites. U.S. Army McAlester provides an engineering benchmark of $74M for a specialized ammunition-process facility plus $21.742M installed equipment; line-equivalent bands are discounted/expanded around that benchmark for Iranian plant complexity. The $1.75B Alabuga Iran-Russia UAV-production contract is used only as a national-scale upper-context check because it includes technology transfer, financing and thousands of UAVs, not pure CAPEX.

envelopes.label: CONSERVATIVE ALL-REGION EXPENDITURE FLOOR
envelopes.quantity_basis: Common all-region Feb. 28–Mar. 31 scope: 6,770 combined launches. Composition case uses 1,234 missiles and 5,536 UAS; see category composition_derivation.
envelopes.methodology: Date-compatible itemized composition floor: 1,234 missiles are directly classified across UAE, Bahrain and Israel; all 2,394 otherwise-unclassified launches are treated as lower-cost UAS for the conservative cost floor.

envelopes.label: CENTRAL MODELED ALL-REGION EXPENDITURE
envelopes.quantity_basis: Common all-region Feb. 28–Mar. 31 scope: 6,770 combined launches. Composition case uses 1,909 missiles and 4,861 UAS; see category composition_derivation.
envelopes.methodology: Date-compatible composition model: apply the pooled missile share in the contemporaneously itemized UAE+Bahrain+Israel sample (1,234 / 4,376 = 28.20%) to the 2,394 unclassified launches, yielding 1,909 missiles and 4,861 UAS.

envelopes.label: ASSESSED UPPER ALL-REGION EXPENDITURE ENVELOPE
envelopes.quantity_basis: Common all-region Feb. 28–Mar. 31 scope: 6,770 combined launches. Composition case uses 2,286 missiles and 4,484 UAS; see category composition_derivation.
envelopes.methodology: Date-compatible upper composition model: apply the highest missile share among the itemized contemporaneous theaters (Israel: 600 / 1,365 = 43.96%) to the 2,394 unclassified launches, yielding 2,286 missiles and 4,484 UAS. This is an upper composition scenario, not a claim that every unclassified theater matched Israel.
exclusions: Potential cheaper SRBMs would lower total.

categories.warning: All three canonical bounds use the same all-region Feb. 28–Mar. 31, 2026 scope of 6,770 combined launches. Composition is derived from date-compatible itemized UAE, Bahrain and Israel missile/UAS splits; the later CSIS 30% missile / 60% drone conflict-wide depletion estimate is context only and is not used to partition the Mar. 31 launch total. The $165.3M Israel-only itemized subset remains a narrower lineage subset, not the all-region low bound.
overlap_notes: Do not merge intentionally expended missile/UAS values with destroyed-inventory quantities for the same item without item-level deconfliction.
This category is reported separately from standing material loss/damage.

narrower_itemized_subset.label: ISRAEL-ONLY ITEMIZED SUBSET — NARROWER SCOPE, NOT AN ALL-REGION LOW BOUND
narrower_itemized_subset.scope: More directly itemized Israel-directed subset in compiled reporting: 600 ballistic missiles + 765 drones.
narrower_itemized_subset.note: Retained for direct/itemized lineage only. It is not the low bound of the all-region munitions-expenditure envelope.

date_compatible_itemized_inputs.note: 433 ballistic + 19 cruise missiles; 1,977 UAVs through Mar. 31.
INSS split reported by Anadolu in the same Apr. 1 compilation.

COMP-LOW-ITEMIZED-MISSILE-FLOOR.formula: Known itemized missiles (1,234); treat all 2,394 unclassified launches as UAS for conservative cost floor.

COMP-HIGH-ISRAEL-MISSILE-SHARE.formula: 1,234 + round(2,394 × (600 / 1,365)) = 2,286 missiles; remainder UAS. Israel is the highest missile-share itemized theater among the contemporaneous inputs.

excluded_stock_depletion_partition.csis_statement: CSIS states Iran expended an estimated 30% of missile inventory and 60% of drones during the conflict.
excluded_stock_depletion_partition.reason: The June report is conflict-wide and published after the June 15 halt; it does not establish that the 30%/60% depletion percentages apply specifically to the Feb. 28–Mar. 31 6,770-launch cutoff.

aggregate_material_loss_summary.currency: USD; mixed 2026 purchasing-power/capability-loss proxies as documented per category
aggregate_material_loss_summary.accounting_scope: Standing material lost, destroyed, or damaged as of the analytical cutoff. Hypothetical future repair/reconstitution spending is excluded.
do_not_sum: MUNITIONS_EXPENDITURE with standing material loss without an explicitly defined combined accounting scope and item-level overlap test
destroyed missile/UAS inventory with intentionally expended weapons where item identity or stock flow is not deconflicted
hypothetical future repair/reconstitution or capability-replacement spending
aggregate_material_loss_summary.interpretation: The low value is a conservative evidence-supported floor, not a claim that every input is imagery-confirmed. The central figure is the preferred modeled standing material-loss estimate. The upper figure is a deliberately broad upper envelope. The missile/UAS inventory category now excludes temporary inaccessibility as full loss and does not monetize an unsupported destroyed-UAS airframe count.
